questions.question_text: Bombs are fired on a bridge such that a probability of a bomb hitting the bridge is 0.5. A minimum of two bombs are required to hit a bridge in order to destroy it. Find the minimum number of hits required such that probability of destroying a bridge is greater than 0.8.
questions.solution_text:
We need the probability of atleast two hits
= 1 - probability of less than two hits
= 1 - (probabilty of 0 hits + probability of 1 hit)
Let n be the number of hits,
Then probability of 0 hits = $(\frac{1}{2})^n$ , since for each turn probability of missing = 1/2
Probability of 1 hit = $n*\frac{1}{2}*(\frac{1}{2})^{n-1}$ = $n*(\frac{1}{2})^n$, since the turn which will hit can be selected in $^nC_1$ ways and probability of hitting in that turn = 1/2 and probability that all other n-1 turns will miss is $(\frac{1}{2})^{n-1}$.
Hence probability of atleast two hits = 1 - $(\frac{1}{2})^n$ - $n*(\frac{1}{2})^n$
The minimum value of n for which the above value is greater than 0.8 is 5

questions.question_text:
If $t>2$, what is the solution set of the inequality

$(t-2)^{t^2 - 6t + 8} > 1$?
questions.solution_text:
Taking logarithm on both sides, we get,
$(t^2 - 6t + 8) log (t-2) > log 1 = 0$
=>$(t - 2)(t - 4) log (t-2) > 0$
For t < 2 and t > 4, (t-2)(t-4) > 0. In this case, for the inequality to hold, log (t-2) > 0
=> t - 2 > 1 => t > 3
The common interval is t > 4
For 2 < t < 4, (t-2)(t-4) < 0. In this case, for the inequality to hold, log (t-2) < 0
=> t - 2 < 1 => t < 3
The common interval is 2 < t < 3
So, the solution set is 2 < t < 3 U t > 4

questions.question_text: One of the roots of the equation $x^2 - (m - 2)x + 6 = 0$ lies between (0, 2) and the other root lies between (3, 4). It is known that $m$ is an integer. What is the sum of all the possible values of $m$?
questions.solution_text:
We know that the graph of a quadratic polynomial cuts x-axis at the points which are also the roots of the quadratic equation. Therefore, the value of the polynomial will be opposite in sign on the two points between which the roots lie.
In this graph, we can observe that the polynomial changes its sign at the roots.
In the given question, one of the roots lie between (0, 2) and the other root lie between (3, 4)
Let $f(x) = x^2 - (m - 2)x + 6$
So, $f(0) > 0$.................(i)
So, $f(2) < 0$.................(i)
So, $f(3) < 0$.................(i)
So, $f(4) > 0$.................(i)
We can write (i) as $6>0$ which is always true
We can write (ii) as
$(14 - 2m) < 0$
$m > 7$
We can write (iii) as
$9-3*(m-2)+6<0$
or $m > 7$
We can write (iv) as
$16-4*(m-2)+6>0$
or, $m<7.5$
Therefore, $m$ belongs to $(7, \dfrac{15}{2})$
Thus, no integral value of $m$ satisfies it.
Hence, option D is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Muthu starts from point A on a circular track with speed 10m/s and meets his friend Vivek after 15 seconds. Now, Muthu and Vivek travel in opposite directions and Vivek reaches Point A in 10 s. Vivek then meets Muthu exactly 14 seconds after crossing point A. Find the circumference of the circular track.
questions.solution_text:
Muthu meets Vivek after 15 seconds with speed 10m/s. Distance covered is 150m.
Vivek  travels till point A in 10s. Hence, Vivek travels at a speed of 15m/s.
When Vivek reaches A, Muthu would have covered a Distance of 100m.
They meet together after 14 seconds. Relative speed is 25m/s. The total distance covered is 25*14=350m.
Circumference= 150+100+350=600m

questions.question_text: The sum of the first 30 terms of an arithmetic progression is equal to the sum of first 48 terms. What is the ratio of the common difference of the AP to 41th term of the same AP?
questions.solution_text:
We have been that
$S_{30}$ = $S_{48}$
=> 15 ( 2a + 29d) = 24(2a + 47d)
=> 30a + 435d = 48a + 1128d
=> 18a + 693d = 0
=> 2a + 77d = 0
We need to find the ratio of the common difference to 41st term.
So we have 
$\frac{d}{a+40d}$
We can write it as 
$\frac{2d}{2a+80d}$
=> $\frac{2d}{2a + 77d + 3d}$
=> $\frac{2d}{ 3d}$ => 2:3
Hence, the required ratio is 2:3

questions.question_text: p, q, r and s are four distinct real numbers such that $p^2 - q = q^2 - r = r^2 - s = s^2 - p$, what is the value of (p + q)(q + r)(r + s)(s + p)?
questions.solution_text:
$p^2 - q = q^2 - r$
$p^2 - q^2 = q - r$
=> $ p + q = \frac{q - r}{p - q}$ -(1)
Similarly, $ q + r = \frac{r - s}{q - r}$(2)
$ r + s = \frac{s - p}{r - s}$ - (3)
$ s + p = \frac{p - r}{s - p}$ - (4)
From (1), (2), (3) and (4) we get (p + q)(q + r)(r + s)(s + p) = $\frac{q - r}{p - q} \times \frac{r - s}{q - r} \times \frac{p - q}{r - s} \times \frac{p - r}{ s - p} = 1$

questions.question_text: There are three solutions A, B and C with acid concentrations as 60%, 40% and 30% respectively. When 100 ml of A is mixed with x ml of B resultant acid concentration is 45% and when 100 ml of A is mixed with y ml of C resultant acid concentration is 40%. When y ml of B is mixed with x ml of C, what is acid concentration in resultant mixture?
questions.solution_text:
$\frac{100\left(0.6\right)+x\left(0.4\right)}{100+x}=\ 0.45$ 
solving we get x = 300 ml
$\frac{100\left(0.6\right)+y\left(0.3\right)}{100+y}=\ 0.4$
solving we get y = 200 ml
resultant concentration = $\frac{200\left(0.4\right)+300\left(0.3\right)}{200+300}$ = $\frac{170}{500}$ = 0.34
Resultant acid concentration = 34%

questions.question_text: What is the absolute difference between the number of 3-digit even numbers that have at least one 2 in them and those that do not have any 2 in them?
questions.solution_text:
Number of 3 digit numbers is 999 - 100 + 1 = 900
Since it starts with an even number and ends with an odd number, it has an equal number of even and odd numbers.
So, the number of even numbers = 900/2 = 450.
Now we need to count the number of even numbers with no 2 in it.
Unit's digit can be filled with any of 0, 4, 6 and 8, since it is an even number and does not contain 2. Count = 4
Ten's digit can have any number from 0 to 9 except for 2. Count = 9
Hundred's digit can have any number from 1 to 9 except for 2. Count = 8
Hence, total number of 3-digit even numbers with no 2 in them = $4\times\ 9\times\ 8=288$
Hence, total number of 3-digit even numbers with at least one 2 in them = 450 - 288 = 162
Hence, difference = 288 - 162 = 126

questions.question_text: A right cylinder of radius = $\sqrt{12}$cm and height = 8 cm is melted and transformed into a cone of same height. If the ratio of lateral surface area of cone to the lateral surface area of cylinder can be represented as a : b$\sqrt{3}$, where a and b are co-primes, what is the value of a + b ?
questions.solution_text:
Since the volume will remain constant, we can equate the volume of cylinder to cone.
$\pi * r^2 * h$ = $\frac{1}{3} * \pi * R^2 *h$
where r is the radius of cylinder and R is the radius of cone
Putting values and solving we get R = 6 cm
So the slant height of cone, l = $\sqrt{6^2 + 8^2}$ = 10 cm
Ratio of lateral surface areas of cone and cylinder = $\frac{\pi Rl}{2\pi rh}$
= $\frac{6 * 10}{2 * \sqrt{12} * 8}$
= $\frac{15}{8\sqrt{3}}$
So, a = 15 and b = 8 and a + b = 23.

questions.question_text: If |x+1|<6 and |y-1|<6 where x,y are integers, what can be the maximum value of x$^{2}$+y$^{2}$-xy
questions.solution_text:
We have, |x+1|<6 and |y-1|<6
|x+1|<6   => -6<x+1<6  =>  -7<x<5
|y-1|<6 => -6< y-1<6 => -5<y<7.
Since x$^{2}$+y$^{2}$ is positive, the value will be maximized when xy is negative.
The highest negative value of x = -6 and highest positive value of y is 6.
Hence the maximum value of x$^{2}$+y$^{2}$-xy will be (-6)$^{2}$+(6)$^{2}$-(-6)(6) = 108

Consider Circle C1 represented by the curve $x^2+y^2-10x-8y+25=0$ and C2 represented by $x^2+y^2-8x-8y+23=0$. The area formed by the tangent common to C1 and C2, a tangent of C2 parallel to x axis and the line y=x+8 is:

A. 32 sq. units

B. 2 sq. units

C. 16 sq. units
questions.solution_text:
C1 is given as: $x^2+y^2-10x-8y+25=0$, which can be re-written as $x^2-10x+25+y^2-8y+16=16$
Or, C1= $\left(x-5\right)^2+\left(y-4\right)^2=4^2$.
C1 has the centre at (5,4) and radius = 4 units.
Similarly, C2 is given as: $x^2+y^2-8x-8y+23=0$, which when manipulated becomes $x^2-8x+16+y^2-8y+16=9$
or, C2 is given as $\left(x-4\right)^2+\left(y-4\right)^2=3^2$, which has a centre at (4,4) and radius 3 units.
The circles, its common tangent, tangents of C2 parallel to X-axis and the line y=x+8 can be drawn as:
The common tangent is represented by the dotted line x=1. The purple line shows y= x+8
The two tangents of the circle C2 are y=1 and y=7.
So, there are two possible triangles formed using the information given in the question, $\triangle ABC\ \ $ and $\triangle ADE\ $
Point C is simply the intersection of y=7 and x=1. So, C=(1,7)
In $\triangle ABC\ \ $, Base AC= 2 units, height BC= 2 units. So, area= $\ \frac{\ 1}{2}\times2\times2=2\ $sq. units
In $\triangle ADE\ $, Base AE= 8 units, Height ED= 8 units. So, area= $\ \frac{\ 1}{2}\times8\times8=32\ $sq. units
therefore both A and B are correct

questions.question_text:
Mohit and Narayan started a company by investing their life savings. The company faced huge losses because of which its value halved. Narayan took out all of his remaining money but Mohit kept on working hard. He made a 300% profit next month. Meanwhile, Narayan found out a scheme of ‘Double your money in 30 days’ and invested half of the money he had left with him. They met at the end of the month and found out they had exactly the same amount of money, as Narayan lost all the money he had invested in the bogus scheme.

If both of them invested money in multiples of Rs. 1000, which of the following can be the total money they had invested in the company initially?
questions.solution_text:
Let the amount Mohit invested be 1000M and that Narayan invested be 1000N Rupees, where M and N are natural numbers.
The value of the company halved. Hence, their investments will also be halved and will become 500M and 500N respectively.
Mohit made a 300% profit the next month. This means, a profit of 3 times 500M. Thus, the final amount with him at the end of the month will be $4\times\ 500M=2000M$.
Narayan lost half of what he had to a bogus scheme. Thus, the total amount with him at the end will be 250N.
It has been given that 2000M=250N. (Money at the end of the month is the same).
Or N=8M.
Total amount in the beginning= 1000M+1000N = 1000M+8000M = 9000M.
Since M is a natural number, the total sum must be a multiple of 9000. Only Option C satisfies this criterion, and hence, is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: An empty tank can be filled in 70 minutes by water flowing from a pipe of square cross section of side 3 cm at the rate of 4 cm/sec. Now another pipe of a circular cross section is added at the bottom of the tank which empties the tank at the rate of 7 cm/sec. When both the pipes are present the tank when empty gets filled completely in 180 minutes. What is the radius of the circular pipe at the bottom of the tank (in cm)?
questions.solution_text:
Volume of flow of water into the tank per second = Rate of flow * Area of cross section of pipe
In first case with only one pipe, Volume flow per sec = $3^2 \times 4$ = 36 units
In second case, Volume flow per sec = 36 - $ \pi r^2\times7$ = 36- $ 7\pi r^2$ units
Ratio of times taken is the inverse ratio of volumes flow per sec
=> $\frac{70}{180}=\frac{36-7\pi r^2}{36}$
Solving, we get r = 1 cm.

questions.question_text: A friend of yours would like to invest an amount of Rs 10000  for a period of 4 years and would want to earn maximum profits and asks for your advice. Which of the following schemes are you most likely to suggest ?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Investing Rs 10000  in  Compound Interest at 20 % p/a for 2 years  followed by investing the amount returned at 10 % p/a  in Simple Interest for two more years .

options.label: B
options.option_text: Investing Rs 10000  in Simple  Interest at 20 % p/a for 2 years followed by investing the amount returned at 10 % p/a in Compound  Interest for two more years .

options.label: C
options.option_text: Investing Rs 10000 in Compound Interest at 15 % p/a for 2 years followed by investing the amount returned at 15 % p/a in Simple Interest for two more years .

options.label: D
options.option_text: Investing Rs 10000  in Simple  Interest at 15 % p/a for 2 years followed by investing the amount returned at 15 % p/a in Simple Interest for two more years .

questions.solution_text:
We need to make sure that he gets maximum return on the Principal of 10000Rs for a period of 4 Years . 
For Simple interest the Amount earned = P(1+RT/100)
For Compound Interest the Amount earned is$P\left(1+\frac{R}{\left(100\right)}\right)^N$ .
Now calculating the Amount received for different options .
Option A : First  Compound interest of  20 percent per annum followed by Simple Interest at 10 percent per annum  :
10000(1.2)(1.2) = 14400 
14000(1 +2*0.1) = Rs 17280 .
Option B : First Simple interest of 20 percent per annum followed by Compound Interest at 10 percent per annum :
10000(1+2*0.2) = 14000
14000(1.1)(1.1) = Rs 16940
Option C : First Compound interest of 15 percent per annum followed by Simple Interest at 15 percent per annum :
10000(1.15)(1.15) = 13225
13225(1+2*0.15) = Rs 17192.5
Option D : First Simple  interest of 15 percent per annum followed by Compound Interest at 15 percent per annum :
10000(1+2*0.15) = 13000
13000(1.15)(1.15) = Rs 17192.5
Option A gives you the maximum returns .

questions.question_text: The sum of the last two digits of $(1^3 + 2^3 + 3^3)^{172}$ is
questions.solution_text:
Let us first evaluate the base of $(1^3 + 2^3 + 3^3)^{172}$ 
= $1^3 + 2^3 + 3^3$ = 36
Now we have to find the last two digits of $36^{172}$
= $6^{344}$
The remainder when $6^{344}$ is divided by 100 is calculated using Chinese remainder theorem.
6 and 100 are not co-prime to each other.
Calculate $6^{344}$ mod 25 and $6^{344}$ mod 4 
$6^{20}$ mod 25 is 1   [From Euler theorem, Euler of 25 = 25*(1-$\frac{1}{5}$) = 20]
$6^{344}$ mod 25 = $6^{340}*6^4$ mod 25 = 1*1296 mod 25  = 36*36 mod 25= 11*11 mod 25 = 121 mod 25 = 21
$6^{344}$ mod 4 is 0
25p+21 = 4q+0
Using trial and error p = 3 and q = 24
25p+21 = 25*3 + 21
=96 is the last two digits of $6^{344}$
Sum of the digits = 15
15 is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Pipe A, pipe B and pipe C are used to fill a tank. The flow rate of pipe C is 25% less than pipe B. To fill the empty tank completely, Pipe A and Pipe B together take one third the time taken by Pipe C alone. If all three pipes can fill the tank in 15 hours, then find the time taken (in hours) by A alone to fill the tank completely.
questions.solution_text:
Assuming the flow rate of pipe A is a  and  that of the pipe B is b, then the flow rate of pipe C = 0.75b
The capacity of the tank = Flow rate of all the tanks*Time taken  = 15(a+b+0.75b) = 15(a+1.75b)
To fill the empty tank completely, pipe A and pipe B together take one-third time than pipe C alone. It means that the flow rate of A and B combined is equal to 3 times that of C.
Hence, a+b  = 3*0.75b
=> a = 1.25b
Hence, the total capacity of the tank = 15(1.25b+1.75b) = 45b
Time taken by A to fill the tank = $\dfrac{45b}{1.25b}\ $  = 36 hours

questions.question_text: PQRS is an isosceles trapezium as shown in the figure. The lengths of the parallel sides are 8 cm and 10cm. The length of the non-parallel side is 8 cm. Which among the following can be the ratio of lengths of one of the parallel sides and the diagonals of the trapezium?
questions.solution_text:
PQRS is an isosceles trapezium and it is inscribed in a circle so it is a cyclic isosceles trapezium.
So all the properties of a cyclic quadrilateral can be applied here.
In an isosceles trapezium, the non-parallel sides are equal.
The diagonals of an isosceles trapezium are equal, so PR = SQ
From Ptolemy Theorem,
PQ*SR+ PS*QR = PR*QS
8*10 +8*8 = PR*PR
PR = 12 cm
The possible ratio of one of the sides and the diagonal = 8:12, 10:12
=2:3, 5:6
B is the correct answer.
